name: Shugaba Abdulrahman Darman v Minister of Internal Affairs
court: Federal Court of Appeal (as then constituted)
summary: A classic case on citizenship, deportation, and freedom of movement - often used to teach how the State cannot casually treat a Nigerian citizen as a deportable alien.
facts: Shugaba Darman, a Nigerian politician, was deported. He challenged the deportation on the basis that he was a Nigerian citizen and that the action violated his fundamental rights.
issues: Whether a Nigerian citizen can lawfully be deported from Nigeria.
How citizenship status interacts with freedom of movement and personal liberty.
holding: The case is taught for the principle that a Nigerian citizen is not liable to deportation in the way an alien may be, and that citizenship findings matter for Chapter IV analysis. Confirm the exact appellate holding in a licensed report.
ratio: Citizenship status is decisive: a person properly shown to be a Nigerian citizen cannot be treated as a deportable alien, and deportation in those circumstances engages fundamental rights protections.
report_citation: See NWLR / law-report citation via a licensed law-report service

interpretations.body: Study tip: separate (1) the factual question of citizenship from (2) the legal consequence once citizenship is established. Then connect to ss.41 and 35 and to modern immigration practice.
